review.market_summary: Three themes matter right now. (1) The US–Iran conflict is escalating in the Gulf. Iran has struck US sites in Kuwait and Bahrain, and the US has hit an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Yet crude (USO -0.9% over 5 days) and defense stocks (ITA -3.8%) have not risen, so either the market doubts the threat to supply or it is waiting for a real disruption. (2) The Fed has turned hawkish. Traders price a 95% chance of a December hike after strong retail sales, Waller has floated a 50bp 'shock', and the dollar is at a 19-month high. Interest-rate-sensitive assets are already falling (ARKK -8%, IWM -4%). (3) Chip export controls are tightening: Nvidia has halted China shipments, and controls now reach Southeast Asian data centers. Semiconductor stocks are already down 5–8% this week, so much of the obvious move has happened. Ahead of the Trump–Xi–Putin summit, trade headlines could swing either way. I'm keeping the book small and avoiding several versions of the same bet.
